patch.value: A quoted final argument makes cmd /s strip the quotes that protect the executable path in the win32 pm launch

pmLaunchPlan launches the win32 .cmd shim as spawnSync(ComSpec, ['/d','/s','/c', bin, ...args], { windowsVerbatimArguments: false }). Node quotes each argv element and joins them into one command tail, so the tail begins with the shim's opening quote. cmd's documented quote handling with /s (the "old behavior", applied unconditionally because /s is present) is: if the first character after /c is a quote, strip that leading quote and remove the LAST quote character on the tail. Whenever the final pm argument itself needs quoting — any tracker root containing a space, e.g. C:\Users\Some User\project — that last quote is an inner one protecting the root, so the strip also destroys the shim's opening quote and the executable path splits at its first space (cmd tries to run C:\Program). Correctness of the launch therefore depends on whether the last argument happens to need quoting, which is why the existing tests (unquoted --json last) passed while real spaced roots break. Found by Greptile review on PR #35 (comment 3789174878, P1, index.ts:892) and confirmed.

value.note: 136 tests pass; new win32 quoting tests: exact outer-wrapped tail for spaced .cmd + quoted final arg, spaced extensionless shim, per-metacharacter CommandLineToArgvW round trip, backslash/quote doubling rules, POSIX argv byte-for-byte unchanged; revert of the outer wrapping alone fails 8 tests

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Exact command tails for a spaced shim path plus a quoted final argument (tracker root `C:\Users\Some User\tracker`), the combination that broke:

BEFORE — Node-quoted discrete argv elements (windowsVerbatimArguments:false), tail as cmd received it:
  cmd.exe /d /s /c "C:\Program Files\pm\node_modules\.bin\pm.cmd" --path "C:\Users\Some User\tracker" list-all --json --include-body
cmd's /s "old behavior": first character after /c is a quote, so strip it and remove the LAST quote character on the tail — here the root's closing quote, not a trailing one:
  C:\Program Files\pm\node_modules\.bin\pm.cmd" --path "C:\Users\Some User\tracker list-all --json --include-body
The executable path loses its quotes and splits at its first space (cmd tries to run `C:\Program`). Worked only when the last argument happened to be unquoted (e.g. bare `--json`), which is why the suite stayed green.

AFTER — the whole tail as ONE argv element, per-element quote-escaped per CommandLineToArgvW, wrapped in an outer pair we add, windowsVerbatimArguments:true so Node adds nothing:
  cmd.exe /d /s /c ""C:\Program Files\pm\node_modules\.bin\pm.cmd" --path "C:\Users\Some User\tracker" list-all --json --include-body"
/s strips exactly the outer pair; the shim stays one quoted token and every inner quote survives. Same mechanism Node itself uses for shell:true on win32, minus the raw string join (no shell:true anywhere).

patch.value:
Fixed: pmLaunchPlan's win32 branch now composes the entire command tail (binary + pm arguments, each quote-escaped per the CommandLineToArgvW rules by quoteWindowsArg) as ONE argv element wrapped in an outer pair of quotes, spawned with windowsVerbatimArguments:true — the same mechanism Node uses for shell:true on win32, without the raw string join. PmLaunch now exposes {command, args(pmArgs), windowsVerbatimArguments} so the executable path and the arguments behind it can never disagree about quoting; POSIX launches are byte-for-byte unchanged (discrete argv, windowsVerbatimArguments:false).

Verified without a Windows box by platform injection: exact outer-wrapped tail asserted for win32 + spaced .cmd + quoted final arg (the broken case), spaced extensionless shim, and ComSpec fallback; per-metacharacter (' ''&''|''<''>''^''('')''"') round trip through a test-local CommandLineToArgvW parser recovers the original argv; backslash-before-quote doubling rules pinned; POSIX argv asserted byte-for-byte. Non-vacuous proof: reverting only the outer-quote wrapping (everything else kept) fails 8 tests, including 'win32 outer-wraps the tail so /s cannot strip the quotes protecting a spaced .cmd path (quoted final arg)'. npm run release:check green; coverage 89.9x/88.9x/91.1x (lines/branches/functions) vs thresholds 83/87/87.

pmLaunchPlan's win32 branch composes the whole command tail (binary + pm arguments, each quote-escaped per the CommandLineToArgvW rules) as ONE argv element wrapped in an outer pair of quotes we add, spawned with windowsVerbatimArguments:true — the mechanism Node itself uses for shell:true on win32, minus the raw string join. /s now strips exactly the outer pair, so the inner quoting that protects the executable path and each argument survives verbatim. PmLaunch carries {command, args(pmArgs), windowsVerbatimArguments} so the path and its quoting are one decision.

A win32 pm read whose shim path or tracker root contains spaces produces a command tail whose only stripped quotes are the outer pair; the .cmd path stays one quoted token and every metacharacter inside an argument reaches pm as data. POSIX launches are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Verified without a Windows box by platform injection: exact outer-wrapped tail asserted for win32 + spaced .cmd + quoted final arg (the previously broken case), spaced extensionless shim, and the ComSpec fallback; per-metacharacter round trip through a test-local CommandLineToArgvW parser recovers the original argv; backslash-before-quote doubling pinned. Non-vacuous: reverting only the outer-quote wrapping fails 8 tests. 136/136 pass; release:check green.
